headline: Sequence models predict chromatin accessibility and variant effects on gene regulation
label: Regulatory Variant Effect Prediction
summary: Single-molecule footprinting and cell-type-resolved sequence models now link DNA sequence and genotype to chromatin and expression readouts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is predicting regulatory readouts from DNA sequence and variants, with increasing resolution at the level of single molecules and single cells. Several preprints fine-tune or extend large sequence-to-function models: Scooby-2 adapts AlphaGenome with a cell-specific decoder for single-cell RNA-seq and chromatin accessibility tracks, and Borzoi is fine-tuned on synthetic MPRA variant-effect labels to improve CAGI5 and eQTL correlations while preserving pre-trained behavior. Variant prioritization is addressed directly by eQIF, which aggregates Enformer predictions into one unsupervised score per common variant, and by an XGBoost-SHAP study of snATAC-seq that prioritizes noncoding SNPs affecting HNF4A binding. Single-molecule work (FiberBrowser and FiberHMM, ChAI-Net, S2d and Mola) models per-molecule chromatin states and co-accessibility from sequence. What is new relative to sequence-only prediction is explicit coupling to cell-type context, as in CellReg3D's integration of DNA language model embeddings with Hi-C 3D chromatin interactions. CUTTIE, a hierarchical testing method for localizing predictive concepts in neural representations, is methodologically distinct from the rest of the set.
